confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear session hijacking event followed by unauthorized cross-departmental data exfiltration. The mid-session IP change is a definitive indicator of hijacking, and the subsequent bulk downloads of sensitive files outside the user's department confirm a successful breach.

attack_chain.description: User_04 logs in from their normal IP (192.168.1.104) within normal hours.
User_04 performs legitimate file reads within the finance department from the normal IP.
Session hijacking occurs: the same session_id (sess_user_04_20260819_001) is used from a new, external IP (91.219.236.222), and the user begins accessing files in the HR department.
The attacker begins bulk downloading sensitive files from multiple departments (Sales, Marketing, Legal, HR) that are outside user_04's authorized scope.

gaps: Geographic location of the second IP (91.219.236.222) to confirm it is not a known VPN used by the employee.
Logs from the authentication server to see if there were any concurrent logins or credential stuffing attempts.
narrative: A session hijacking incident occurred when user_04's active session was hijacked by an external IP (91.219.236.222). The attacker leveraged this session to perform unauthorized cross-departmental file access and exfiltrate a large volume of sensitive data from the HR, Sales, Marketing, and Legal departments.
